pairs.subject: lead-quality-and-source-diagnosis
pairs.evidence: src/lib/lead-quality/compute.ts:308 Cost-per-qualified-lead drift alerts and junk source flags are evaluated without checking minimum sample thresholds, allowing small-count noise to trigger warnings and negative classifications.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/lead-quality/compute.ts:49 Computes composite 0-100 quality score by weighting qualification rate (0.6) and win rate (0.4) on adjacent denominators.
src/lib/lead-quality/compute.ts:50 Flags a paid source as junk based solely on qualification rate below 0.35 without checking whether the lead count clears the sample floor.
src/lib/lead-quality/compute.ts:308 Raises a CPQL rise drift alert on relative delta without checking whether current or prior periods clear a minimum qualified lead sample floor.

techniques.evidence: src/components/app/modules/LeadQualityModule.tsx:259 Renders undefined ROI on unpaid lead sources as infinity rather than rendering the absent metric as absent or null.

pairs.subject: lead-quality-and-source-diagnosis
pairs.evidence: src/lib/ai/tools/lead-source-diagnosis.ts:160 The tool splits spam from mis-targeting using an uncalibrated absolute currency constant rather than evaluating cost per lead relative to peer sources and prior period history.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/ai/tools/lead-source-diagnosis.ts:170 Follows the prescribed taxonomy and order in the deterministic fallback: volume sample gate first, then qualification split, win rate, and paid pricing.
src/lib/ai/tools/lead-source-diagnosis.ts:160 Hardcodes an absolute currency threshold (200 CZK) for cheap CPL instead of computing cheapness relative to peer median and prior-period baseline.
src/lib/ai/tools/lead-source-diagnosis.ts:175 Diagnoses a win rate failure (mis-targeting) without enforcing a stage-specific sample floor on the qualified lead count.

pairs.registryProposal: cheap-cpl-splits-spam-from-mistargeting requires comparing CPL against peer median and prior period, but does not specify a fallback rule when a project has zero or one peer sources and no prior period; specifying the single-source cold-start behavior would prevent implementations from falling back to hardcoded currency constants.

declined.subject: lead-quality-and-source-diagnosis
declined.reason: The subject lead-quality-and-source-diagnosis owns source quality scoring, junk source detection, source-level root cause diagnosis, and two-axis fit-engagement lead scoring for queues. Per the golden path standard lines 26-30, speed-to-lead owns the reply clock, qualifying questions, and assisted reply drafting after a lead arrives (subject speed-to-lead-and-assisted-reply). speed-lead-ui implements the response-SLA clock and BANT qualification UI for speed-to-lead, not source quality scoring or source diagnosis.
